text:
Recent work supports learning behavioral relationships alongside text semantics, rather than treating lexical similarity as next-item relevance. [CoCoRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12183) combines textual and collaborative information through semantic codes, cross-attention, and masked alignment objectives. [LLM2Rec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.21579) explicitly trains text representations to capture interaction-derived item relationships. Both provide conceptual motivation; neither establishes an effective small encoder trained entirely from scratch under the stated constraints.

For substitutes versus complements, [TransGAT (ICDM 2024)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10884336/) uses distinct key/value representations to model behavioral direction and non-transitive complementarity, jointly learning substitute and complement graphs. Earlier [Knowledge-aware Complementary Product Representation Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.12574) likewise motivates separate item-in/item-out embeddings for asymmetric relationships. These mechanisms suggest directed scoring rather than symmetric text similarity. However, the benchmark supplies no verified relationship labels: observed transitions cannot establish substitution, complementarity, or product compatibility.

A constraint-compatible experiment, proposed here rather than validated by these papers: randomly initialize a token-embedding mean-pooling encoder or small CNN over permitted titles/descriptions; learn separate source/target projections using training-only transitions and a sampled next-item ranking loss; combine its score with SASRec through a learned gate. Compare against lexical overlap, ID-only directed transitions, and symmetric text scoring. For user-disjoint diagnostics, fit auxiliary transition representations without diagnostic users, then compare against representations including their histories; remove each user’s contributed transition counts when testing count-based shortcuts. Report performance by transition support and item frequency. Select using the prescribed four-category macro validation HR@10; describe gains as predictive association, without compatibility claims.
